building: buildingId is the id the building reads use: a physical_features row whose body kind is 'building'
Its site is map_areas.site_id of its area. map_areas.site_id is UNIQUE (database/sql/20-area/area.sql),
so a site has one area, and that area can hold several buildings.
snapshot: usp_snapshots has one writer, captureRegistrySnapshotTx (usp/snapshots.ts:150-204); scope_id is the site
snapshotRows (snapshots.ts:70-148) captures every physical_features row of the site with revision > 0
(:90-97) whatever the selection: a 'targets' selection only requires its pins to be among those rows
Each captured row is a manifest member { pin: { ref: { namespace, id }, revision }, bodySha256, bodyRef,
authority } (:56, :170-178). A feature has namespace 'area_feature' and its own id.
rule: A snapshot is of this building when both hold: usp_snapshots.scope_id equals the building's site id, and
the stored manifest lists a member whose pin ref is { namespace: 'area_feature', id: buildingId }.
The member revision is not compared. The list says which recorded snapshots hold the building, each at
the revision it captured; newest-first order is the only statement about recency.
canTheStoredBodyTell: Yes. Members are listed by reference in the stored body, so the read needs no containsBuilding field and
siteSnapshotWithoutTheBuilding: Omitted. It was captured when the building was not recorded (absent, or still at revision 0), so its
scope cannot answer a read about this building: resolveRegistryTarget answers target_not_in_snapshot for
it. Listing it would hand the client a scope the next read refuses.

A building still at revision 0 answers 200 with no items, because no capture can list it.

storedBodyThatFailsTheSchema: Skipped and counted. A selected row whose body fails UspSnapshotManifestSchema, or whose stored scope
does not name its own row (id, scope_id, digest), is left out of items and counted in a top-level
'unreadable' number. Items keep one shape, so items[n].scope can always be passed on. Only rows the page
statement selected are counted (same site, access view, policy and member), so the number reveals no
controller: A new BuildingSnapshotsController in the register module (apps/api/src/modules/register), rooted at
api/v1/buildings beside BuildingLedgerController, with its line in that module's operation-manifest.json
Why there: the path is a building path, and the building's own check must answer the neighbouring 404
body. Register controllers answer through the global ApiExceptionFilter ({ error: { code, message,
requestId } }); the USP controllers add EvidenceExceptionFilter, whose body carries 'retryable' and
would differ from the ledger, register and canonical 404.
The USP admission lives in no controller: it is assertLocalUsp(ctx) in the domain function, with ctx
from localRequestContext (usp/principal.ts), built from the request id as the USP controllers build it.
The response is the plain document, as the other building reads answer. A USP envelope carries one
